title: Security onramp: Silver Lining inference deployment options
summary: Introductory security discovery for Silver Lining's plan to surface LLM features in clinical workflows. Customer asked about SOC 2 timeline, ISO27001, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs retention, and KMS integration for private deployment. Redwood AE/SE walked through hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and logging/KMS options. Agreed to share SOC2 report, network diagram template, and an initial cost/latency tradeoff doc; bench pilot proposed.
topics: SOC2 and ISO27001 status and evidence
SSO / SAML integration and IdP requirements
Encryption at rest / KMS key options (hosted vs customer-managed)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Data retention & purging for PHI-adjacent logs
action_items: Jared Kim - Send SOC2 report link and current cert dates - 2027-04-23
Priya Patel - Prepare short latency/cost comparison for hosted vs dedicated for their seq lengths - 2027-04-27
Alex Chen - Share current IdP SAML metadata and required attributes - 2027-04-22
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and network diagram template
Schedule pilot kickoff (benchmarks + sample prompts) if legal okay
Set up follow-up technical deep dive with Silver Lining infra team week of Apr 26
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-20 16:00 PDT / Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Silver Lining - Head of Security), Maya Singh (SRE Lead), Tom Alvarez (Legal), Nina Park (Eng Manager)

Summary: quick intros then jump into security requirements; customer is evaluating whether to go hosted first or go private from day one due to regulatory and PHI-adjacent telemetry. Lots of questions about key management and auditability.

00:00 Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jared with Redwood inference, I'm the AE on this account, and with me are Priya and Carlos - SEs - they're gonna take the technical bits, but I'll run us through timeline and next steps.
00:12 Alex: Hey thanks, Alex here, head of security at Silver Lining. Quick context: we are building an internal assistant for clinicians, not storing PHI in the model but some PII and clinical codes may appear in logs. We need to understand compliance boundaries.
00:34 Priya: Yeah thanks Alex. Can you say a little more about the workload? Token lengths, expected qps, and whether you're looking at streaming responses or batch?
00:42 Nina: Mostly short prompts, 200-400 tokens typically, occasional longer context up to 2k tokens for case history. QPS low to medium, 5-20 rps surface area. We are prototyping with hosted but legal is nervous.
01:03 Carlos: got it. So two main threads: security/compliance (SOC2/ISO/SAML/KMS) and deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private). We'll cover both.
01:17 Tom: quick question about PHI — we won't consent to any third-party access to PHI, so we'd need guarantees on data handling plus contractual terms.
01:28 Jared: Understood. On the data plane we offer options: hosted with strict retention and opt-in customer controls, dedicated reserved pools, or private (VPC/air-gapped) for full isolation. Each has different KMS options.
01:44 Alex: What's Redwood's SOC2 posture? Do you have an ISO27001 cert? We need certs and dates for security review board.
01:52 Priya: We're SOC2 Type II certified; current report covers up to Feb 2027, we'll share the attestation. For ISO: we're working toward ISO27001, targeted Q3 2027, not certified yet.
02:07 Maya: ok can you also clarify whether audit logs include request/response bodies? We need to make sure PHI isn't captured in logs by default.
02:18 Priya: Good question; default logging captures metadata and tokens counts, also request IDs and model used; payload capture is off by default for hosted — we retain only minimal traces unless customer enables full transcript logging for debugging. For private deployments you control log exports entirely.
02:42 Alex: So for hosted, is there an option for customer-managed KMS so logs and snapshots are encrypted under our key?
02:50 Carlos: For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default; we also provide a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise plans where we can integrate with AWS KMS/GCP CMEK. For Dedicated, CMEK is available and for Private you manage keys on-prem.
03:10 Tom: How about SSO? We use Okta, need SAML 2.0 with specific attributes and SCIM for provisioning. Also RBAC: we need separation of duties between dev, infra, and compliance.
03:23 Priya: We support SAML 2.0 IdP integration, Okta works fine; we also support SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based with custom roles for higher tiers. We'll share a mapping doc for default roles and can scope token scoping to route-level access.
03:42 Alex: Audit log retention — what are the default retention windows and can we export logs off-platform?
03:49 Carlos: Default retains 90 days for detailed request logs on hosted; you can configure longer retention for Dedicated/Private and export logs to your SIEM (S3, BigQuery) via a push or pull. We can also provide near real-time streaming of events for monitoring.
04:06 Maya: We need sub-second latency for interactive clinician flows; can you quantify latency differences across deployment modes for our typical token lengths?
04:15 Priya: Rough numbers: hosted avg p95 for 200-400 tokens ~ 120-200ms, dedicated reserved pools can hit p95 ~ 80-150ms depending on GPU family and batch settings, private on-prem depends heavily on infra — we provide guidance. We'll run benchmarks in pilot.
04:36 Alex: Any chance of model output being used for training? We need to be sure Redwood doesn't use customer data to improve models unless contractually permitted.
04:45 Jared: Redwood does not use customer payloads to train models. We'll put that in the data processing addendum — default is no training on customer data.
04:55 Tom: About encryption at rest and in transit? Compliance wants AES-256 for at-rest and TLS 1.2+ for transit.
05:03 Priya: We encrypt in transit with TLS 1.2/1.3 and at rest using AES-256; for hosted keys we use provider KMS with rotating keys, and for customer-managed KMS we support rekeying schedules.
05:22 Alex: Are audit logs tamper-evident? Chain of custody?
05:26 Carlos: We can append logs to an immutable storage (e.g., WORM S3) or ship to your SIEM with signatures. Our console also has immutability flags for export.
05:40 Maya: What about data residency — we need EU data to stay in eu-west1 region, is that supported on hosted?
05:47 Jared: Yes, region pinning is supported for hosted and dedicated customers; Private naturally stays in your region. We'll capture your primary region for contract.
06:02 Nina: Any recommendations for retention windows for debugging vs compliance? We want short-term full payload retention for debugging, long-term metadata-only retention for audits.
06:12 Priya: That's our recommended pattern — short TTL (7-30 days) for full transcripts, then metadata-only for 1-3 years depending on regs. We can automate purging and provide attestations.
06:29 Alex: Onboarding timeline — our security board meets May 5th. Ideally we'd have SOC2 docs, network diagram, and SAML metadata by then.
06:38 Jared: We can get SOC2 and network diagram over by Apr 23 and set a follow-up deep dive. If they like what they see, pilot could start late May.
06:48 Tom: For legal, we need a DPA draft and clarity on log retention terms.
06:53 Jared: We'll include a DPA template and the data handling addendum in the package.
07:00 Carlos: A few technical notes: for KV cache and prefix caching, we can mask prompts to avoid storing sensitive tokens; we also support dynamic masking in the runtime for PHI tokens, which helps with compliance.
07:18 Maya: interesting, how reliable is masking? false negatives are a concern.
07:22 Priya: Masking is heuristic-driven; for high assurance we recommend tokenization + predetermined scrub lists plus pipeline post-processors and to route sensitive prompts to private deployment. We'll include recommended scrub flows.
07:42 Alex: Competitors question — we've also looked at OtherAI Inc and CloudProviderX. How do you compare especially on logging and dedicated private key options?
07:52 Jared: high level — Redwood focuses on inference economics and observability; we provide dedicated pools and private deployment with full key control, and we surface auditability features built-in. We'll share a concise comparison doc.
08:05 Nina: Next steps recap?
08:09 Jared: Sure - I'll send SOC2, network diagram template, DPA draft. Priya will prepare latency/cost deck and runbook for masking and KMS options. We'll schedule a tech deep dive w/ infra for the week of Apr 26. Alex/Tom to share SAML metadata and list of required attributes.
08:30 Alex: sounds good, thanks all.
08:33 Jared: thanks everyone, we can end there.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional phrase drops and proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., KMS provider names, some latencies rounded).
